documents.title: AI in Teaching: Communicate about AI
documents.summary: Tier 4. USU teaching guidance requiring instructors to define AI guidelines in the syllabus and enforce them under Article VI of the Student Code. It describes three broad categories of course policy, from prohibited (which explicitly covers coding assistants) to encouraged, with template statements on detection, sanctions, citation and acknowledgement. It also asks instructors to disclose their own AI use, such as for grading feedback.

documents.summary: Tier 1. Spring 2026 syllabus for UNLV's required computing ethics course. Students are responsible for their submitted work whatever tools they used, must openly acknowledge any generative AI content or translation (tool name and marked passages), and must keep the full AI output until the end of term. Exams are closed-book with devices off.

documents.unit: Center for Effective Teaching and Learning (CETL)
documents.title: Recommendations for Teaching & Learning with AI
documents.summary: Tier 4. CETL guidance for Cal State LA faculty. AI misuse falls under existing plagiarism standards, but instructors are urged to write their own policy, whether a ban, full use or a middle path, covering examples, rationale, citation and consequences, and possibly co-created with students. The page explains that the campus switched off Turnitin's AI detector and notes detector bias against non-native English writers.
